content.title: A pipeline of small pure-Go packages
content.lede: gowkhtmltopdf is a clean-room work-alike of wkhtmltopdf: HTML is loaded, parsed, laid out, paginated, and painted into a PDF 1.4 document (or a PNG/JPEG bitmap) using the Go standard library plus two allowlisted pure-Go modules for OpenType shaping and SVG rasterization.

content.heading: Package map
rows: Command-to-engine adapters that keep `internal/convert` CLI-independent for library callers
URL guess, HTTP(S)/file/`data:` loading, ACL, cookies, auth, POST
Allowlisted HTML tokenizer and element tree
Style resolve, block/inline/table layout, display list, paint
Headings to outline tree and dump XML
PDF job orchestration: header/footer, TOC, links, copies
PDF 1.4 writer, TTF subset, images, annotations
SVG-as-image rasterization for `` via tdewolff/canvas

sections.heading: 1. Parse CLI or library settings
sections.body: `internal/cli` turns argv into a `Command` (or the root package builds converter state directly). Every option lands in `internal/settings` as a dotted name such as `page.size` or `margin.left`, readable with the same `Get` / `Set` API the library exposes.

sections.heading: 2. Load each body object
sections.body: `internal/load.Loader` guesses the URL scheme, fetches HTML from HTTP(S), a local file, or a `data:` URL, and applies the ACL, cookies, auth, and POST settings. Each object in the multi-document grammar (`page`, `cover`, `toc`) is loaded independently.

sections.heading: 3. Parse HTML and CSS
sections.body: `internal/html` tokenizes into an allowlisted element tree. `internal/css` parses the supported CSS subset, runs selectors against the tree, and produces the cascade used in the next stage.
bullets: Inline and linked style sheets are merged when the content policy allows them.

sections.heading: 4. Layout
sections.body: `internal/layout` resolves computed styles, lays out blocks, inline content, and tables, and emits a display list of ops (text runs, rects, images, links). SVG images are rasterized by `internal/svg` before they enter the display list.

sections.heading: 5. Paginate
sections.body: The display list is split into pages using `page.size`, the four margins, and `page-break-*` CSS hints.

sections.heading: 6. Paint
sections.body: `internal/convert` feeds the paginated ops into `internal/pdf`, which paints them onto `pdf.Document` pages with the embedded font subset and image xobjects.

sections.heading: 7. TOC
sections.body: When a TOC object is present, `internal/outline` builds the heading tree and `internal/convert` runs the two-iteration page-count fixpoint so TOC page numbers settle before final placement.

sections.heading: 8. Reorder
sections.body: TOC pages are moved ahead of the body pages when a TOC is requested, matching wkhtmltopdf output ordering.

sections.heading: 9. Annotations and final pass
sections.body: `internal/outline` and `internal/pdf` attach the document outline, link annotations, and header/footer content in a final pass, then the Catalog references the outline root.

sections.heading: 10. Write
sections.body: `internal/pdf` writes the file: zlib Flate streams, the TTF font subset, and a correct xref table, producing a PDF 1.4 document.

content.heading: PDF writer notes
items: Targets PDF 1.4, written in pure Go with no native dependencies.
Fonts are an embedded Liberation Sans subset: a simple font with WinAnsi-style Latin-1 codes, `/Widths` expressed in 1000 units per em.
Outlines get the Catalog `/Outlines N 0 R` entry assigned only after the outline object references exist.
CJK and complex-script output uses the Type0/CID path with `--font-path`, without HarfBuzz shaping.

content.title: Image mode reuses the same front end
content.body: `ImageConverter` shares stages 1 through 4 (load, parse, layout). Instead of painting into `internal/pdf`, `internal/imageout` rasterizes the display list with a bitmap font and encodes PNG or JPEG, so the two binaries stay behaviorally aligned on parsing and layout.

sections.heading: Local access is denied by default
sections.body: The loader refuses local file access unless `--enable-local-file-access` (or the equivalent setting) is passed. `--allow` prefixes opt in selective local paths.
bullets: HTTP loading enforces connect and response timeouts, a maximum redirect count, and a maximum body size.
The full threat model is documented in THREAT-MODEL.md.

sections.heading: Extension points are intentionally small
sections.body: The public API is settings-driven (dotted names), not a plugin framework. New CSS properties or elements require changes inside `internal/css` and `internal/layout` plus an update to the compatibility matrix.
